record.paper_title: PROGRESS IN THE OPEN PROBLEMS IN THEORY OF FUNCTIONS OF BOUNDED INDEX
record.original_question: Let b_1,b_2 ∈ C^2 be directions, let g(z_1,z_2) be an entire function of bounded L-index in the directions b_1 and b_2, and interpret bounded L^*-index in a direction b^* by the same directional-derivative criterion as above, with L replaced by L^* and b replaced by b^*. Determine a positive continuous function L^* and a direction b^* such that every entire solution F of the mixed-derivative equation ∂^2F/(∂b_1 ∂b_2) = g(z_1,z_2) has bounded L^*-index in the direction b^*.

evidence.quote: An entire function F(z), z ∈ C^n, is called ([11, 12]) a function of bounded L-index in a direction b = (b1, . . . , bn) ∈ C^n \ {0}, if there exists m0 ∈ Z+ such that for every m ∈ Z+ and every z ∈ C^n ...

Problem 2 ([10, Problem 2]). Let g(z1, z2) be an entire function of bounded L-index in the directions b1 and b2. What are a function L* and a direction b* that an entire solution of equation ∂^2F/∂b1∂b2 = g(z1, z2) has a bounded L*-index in the direction b*?
This means that the problem also requires initial conditions to certainly describe behavior of entire solutions.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For a nonzero direction $b=(b_1,\dots,b_n)\in\mathbb{C}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and a positive continuous function $L:\mathbb{C}^n\to(0,\infty)$, an entire function $F:\mathbb{C}^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is said to have bounded $L$-index in the direction $b$ if there exists $m_0\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ such that for every $m\in\mathbb{Z}_+$ and every $z\in\mathbb{C}^n$,
$$\frac{|\partial_b^m F(z)|}{m!\,L(z)^m}\le\max_{0\le k\le m_0}\frac{|\partial_b^k F(z)|}{k!\,L(z)^k},$$
where $\partial_b F(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n b_j\,\partial F/\partial z_j$ and $\partial_b^m$ denotes the $m$-fold iterate. The same definition with $L,b$ replaced by $L^*,b^*$ defines bounded $L^*$-index in direction $b^*$.

Problem. Let $n=2$ and let $b_1,b_2\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$ be two given directions. Suppose $g:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ is an entire function having bounded $L$-index in each of the directions $b_1$ and $b_2$ (for some positive continuous $L$). Determine a positive continuous function $L^*:\mathbb{C}^2\to(0,\infty)$ and a direction $b^*\in\mathbb{C}^2\setminus\{0\}$, possibly together with appropriate initial conditions, such that every entire solution $F:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}$ of the mixed-derivative equation
$$\partial_{b_1}\partial_{b_2} F(z_1,z_2)=g(z_1,z_2)$$
has bounded $L^*$-index in the direction $b^*$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem belongs to a program on bounded L-index in direction and PDEs. Related results exist (e.g., for second-order PDEs entire solutions are shown to have bounded L-index in a direction under suitable hypotheses), but a definitive solution to this specific mixed-derivative problem in two prescribed directions was not located in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Boundedness of the L-index in a direction of entire solutions of second order partial differential equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies boundedness of L-index in a direction for entire solutions of certain second order PDEs.
status_evidence.claim: Related partial progress exists for second-order PDEs but not specifically resolving the mixed-derivative problem with two arbitrary directions.

status_evidence.title: Entire Functions of Bounded L-Index: Its Zeros and Behavior of Partial Logarithmic Derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of entire functions of bounded L-index, with applications to differential equations.
status_evidence.claim: The framework is active but a complete answer to the stated mixed-derivative problem was not found.
